robot: Mini Pupper v4 SKU2 (long body, Raspberry Pi 5), MD01 servo modules
measured: robot on its stand, legs moved by hand with the servos limp (positions from the servos' potentiometers at 200 Hz); abduction stops confirmed under power (5 deg/s, duty <= 0.6)

conventions.units: degrees from the stand pose (the calibrated neutral pose)
conventions.knee_fold: knee relative to the thigh, + = folding; the knee servo (inner coaxial output) must turn with the hip to hold a knee angle, so its limit is on the knee-thigh angle, not on the servo
conventions.track_end: the potentiometer's electrical track (310 deg) ends; a ~50 deg dead zone lies beyond. Not a mechanical stop, but positions there are unreadable: keep powered motion >= 20 deg inside. Depends on how each joint is mounted and calibrated
conventions.model_joint_range_rad: the same limits as joint ranges of the robot model (joints *_hip = abduction, *_calf = knee relative to the thigh), absolute angles (stand + measured range)

findings: Abduction has 38-45 deg of travel in total (14-22 inward, 23-28 outward), limited by the chassis.
The knee's range relative to the thigh is about 120 deg (mirrored left/right).

The hip turns to the pot's track ends both ways when the abduction is near neutral; near either abduction extreme the chassis stops the thigh swinging towards the body's middle (backward on front legs, forward on rear legs).

model_joint_range_rad.FR_thigh_note: no fixed range: the chassis stop depends on the abduction (a collision, not a joint limit); otherwise the pot's track ends (mounting-dependent)

legs.source: hand; the Pi's and the bench supply's connectors obstructed the backward hip swing: its middle and outward-abduction backward limits are mirrored from FR
